caller: actual public stdio MCP server, interface_observe, interface_validate, interface_dispatch
target: two sequentially owned fixture_app processes, one configured fixture HWND per MCP server process
procedure: Start owned fixture process A and obtain its Win32 target generation from public interface_observe receipt.
Close process A and verify its HWND is destroyed and process exits.
Start distinct owned fixture process B and verify its target generation differs from A.
Submit one syntactically valid focused text program through public interface_validate and interface_dispatch, carrying process A generation while server B is configured for process B.
Require TARGET_GENERATION_CHANGED before session dispatch; independently check B event journal contains no input-caused events and no task effect file exists.
input_scope: The only proposed action is one sentinel text payload addressed to owned fixture B. It must be refused before emission; if the guard fails, only the owned fixture can receive it. No pre-existing application is configured or targeted.
retry_policy: One frozen trial only. Any timeout, ambiguous receipt, cleanup uncertainty, or failed check remains FAIL/UNKNOWN and is not replayed.
cleanup: Post WM_CLOSE only to owned fixture HWNDs, wait boundedly, and terminate/kill only their owned process if close fails; preserve all output.
acceptance: Public interface_observe succeeds and exposes a stable lowercase SHA-256 target_generation in its raw report.
Two distinct fixture process identities produce distinct target generations.
Public static validation accepts the caller program.
Public dispatch is attempted exactly once and returns TARGET_GENERATION_CHANGED with input_dispatched=false; fixture B records no character events.
Fixture B records only its initial ready event, no chars/click/save, no effect file exists, and both owned processes exit cleanly with HWNDs destroyed.
nonclaims: atomic check/use or window-lifetime fencing after admission
native input delivery, release, blocked-I/O bounds, or recovery
task effect, MAP01, model efficiency, or reliability
